nodes.label: The shared-memory pixel path
nodes.rationale: Commands cover 95% of what the system draws; this is the other 5% - apps that produce pixels, where commands are no use and you drop down to shared memory. A different path that has to be designed separately.

nodes.label: Pixels do not live in Lua tables
nodes.rationale: 2 million pixels as a Lua table is over 32 MB for an 8 MB image, and worse, the GC walks 2 million slots every cycle. No optimisation saves that; it is structural. Lua tables carry intent, never pixels.

nodes.label: The surface userdata
nodes.rationale: An opaque handle over a flat block of bytes the GC does not traverse, only frees. The handle travels inside the commit table as a capability rather than as data, so the protocol is still tables.

nodes.label: The small composable C primitive set
nodes.rationale: fill, blit, blend, span, get/set and map: Lua decides what to do and C does it per pixel, because a full-screen filter in Lua is 40-100 ms. The triangle rasteriser and Doom's blitter are each one more primitive, not an exception to the model.

nodes.label: map, the slow escape hatch
nodes.rationale: It allows any filter without adding primitives and is slow on purpose: something using map that needs to be fast is the signal it deserves its own C primitive, and only then is one added.

nodes.label: Pitch and format travel with the handle
nodes.rationale: No line of Lua may compute a pixel offset; the userdata holds w, h, pitch, fmt and bytes per pixel, and address arithmetic happens only in C. App surfaces are always the canonical format, so a new target changes one file. A pitch bug is invisible from inside the process - every read agrees with every write - so its test has to live outside the guest.

nodes.label: Double buffering and an explicit commit
nodes.rationale: No locks, so every shared surface has two buffers and an index of which is live; the app draws into the other and commits. Damage is a field of the commit rather than a separate call, which makes it hard to forget, and an app that does not commit never freezes the compositor.

nodes.label: Cache coherency before the blit
nodes.rationale: Inner shareable rather than a manual DC CVAC over megabytes a frame, which costs more than bus coherency and is a source of forgotten bugs. The attributes of a shared surface are decided at creation in the kernel and never touched; if a Lua cache-invalidation API is needed, something was designed wrong.

nodes.label: The GC does not see surface memory
nodes.rationale: Lua sees 40 bytes behind which there are 8 MB, so it feels no pressure and does not collect - the process dies on OOM while collectgarbage('count') reports 200 KB. Explicit free is the expected path, __gc the net, and the allocation tells the GC the real size.

nodes.label: The full path, top to bottom
nodes.rationale: Eight steps and two IPC crossings, not one of them carrying a pixel inside a Lua table. If the Lua steps ever show up in a profile, a pixel loop has crept into Lua.

nodes.label: Who frees a shared surface's pages
nodes.rationale: A region is refcounted and its pages go back when the last capability drops, not when a process that mapped it exits. The rule is an address range rather than a flag on a page: shared regions map at USER_SHARE_VA, a window nothing frees by walking. Both bump pointers need a ceiling, and shared pages are charged once, to whoever created the region.

nodes.label: What a Lua/C crossing costs
nodes.rationale: About 9 microseconds, which buys about two thousand pixels - so a 30-pixel span is 99% overhead and a 32x32 tile is break-even. A primitive should write about two thousand pixels or be called in a batch. The same disc is 3 Mpx/s span-per-row from Lua and 103 Mpx/s as one call.

nodes.label: gfxbench
nodes.rationale: Measures the primitives under QEMU: fill 214 Mpx/s, blit 48, span 80. The number is QEMU's; the ratio between the rows is what transfers.

nodes.label: Doom, the ideal shape
nodes.rationale: It renders a frame inside its own C loop and hands over one buffer: one crossing per frame rather than one per shape. The headroom is not the interesting part - the shape is.

nodes.label: Outline fonts, and why there are three faces
nodes.rationale: The bitmap font stays the default because it is exact and costs nothing. ui, text and mono want different things and the terminal's must be fixed-width, which is not a preference. Five faces took the user image from 577 KB to 1433 KB, and every process gets a private copy - about 19.6 MB spent on the same bytes fourteen times, which is a property of the image rather than of fonts.

nodes.label: stb_truetype
nodes.rationale: Vendored unmodified, handling TrueType and CFF. Its own header says it offers no security guarantee against untrusted font files; what contains it today is where it runs - EL0, in whichever process is drawing - and that stops being sufficient the moment fonts arrive from somewhere other than the build.

nodes.label: The font server that is not built yet
nodes.rationale: The weak argument is duplication, which shared read-only image pages fix instead. The real argument is the parser: an untrusted file parsed in fourteen address spaces becomes one process that can die and be restarted. Glyph-per-IPC is not allowed at 9us a crossing, so the server owns the faces and hands out an atlas per (face, size) as a shared region.

nodes.label: The graphics build order
nodes.rationale: Surface, primitives, free/__gc done at M6; sharing with the app server, double buffering and commit with damage, inner shareable attributes and map at M7; the triangle rasteriser at M9.
